source.title: Grokking at the Edge of Numerical Stability
source.authors: Lucas Prieto; Melih Barsbey; P. Mediano; Tolga Birdal

record.tranche_reason: The study presents experiments and an account of delayed generalization that refine the grokking claim, including evidence that Softmax numerical errors can stop learning and that avoiding them changes outcomes.
record.gate_note: Cited findings from prior work are not recorded as results. Results in the realistic-data section comparing the authors’ methods are omitted where they report method performance but do not measure delayed generalization. The Fourier-weight plot reports structure, not gradual formation of a generalizing circuit or a continuous progress measure.
record.test_reason: The study trains MLPs and one-layer transformers on modular arithmetic and sparse parity, plus MLPs on MNIST, under controlled numerical and optimizer changes. It argues the claim needs restating. Softmax floating-point errors (Softmax Collapse) stop generalization rather than create the delay. The delay itself comes from logit scaling under cross-entropy (naive loss minimization). Removing that scaling with ⊥Grad, or using compact binary inputs, removes the delay.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly right, but it blurs two roles. The authors attribute the delay to naive loss minimization (cross-entropy logit scaling after overfitting). They attribute the absence of grokking without regularization to Softmax Collapse from floating-point absorption errors, which halts learning. StableMax (or higher precision) avoids Collapse and enables grokking without regularization. ⊥Grad removes the delay by projecting out the logit-scaling gradient component. They also argue weight decay works by countering this scaling.
record.recipe_differences: The study uses modular arithmetic tasks and related accuracy trajectories, but focuses on interventions to Softmax computation, floating-point precision, and gradient projection rather than reproducing the original grokking recipe. It also studies sparse parity and MNIST.
record.method_sensitivity: Outcomes vary with dataset size and floating-point precision; the study also reports effects of input representation, weight decay, optimizer, and loss/Softmax choice.

fits_no_version.finding: StableMax-induced grokking without weight decay occurs while the L2 weight norm rises substantially.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Grokking does not require a decreasing weight norm or a low-norm bias.

fits_no_version.finding: An MLP that groks without weight decay (via StableMax) shows Fourier sparsity in its output weights similar to Nanda et al. (Fig. 12).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Fourier structure can emerge without a weight-decay-driven cleanup phase.

fits_no_version.finding: Artificially zeroing correct-class gradients at epoch 6000 halts generalization in a model that otherwise generalizes.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Zero correct-class gradients (as under Softmax Collapse) are sufficient to stop grokking.

record.problems: Many central accuracy and Collapse results are presented in plots without exact values in the text. The study’s numerical-instability findings are tested in particular architectures and tasks; the authors note that formalizing their account for quasi-homogeneous models remains future work.
record.rows_left_out: No qualifying result rows were omitted. Figure 12’s Fourier-component plot is not a test of gradual circuit formation or a continuous progress measure, so it is not included as a V2 result. Realistic-data method comparisons are not recorded as delayed-generalization outcomes.

untested.parts: A measured relation between delay length and training-set size. Fig. 2 shows smaller splits fail to generalize at all without regularization; it does not show longer delays.
Not tested. Fig. 12 (Fourier sparsity without weight decay) is described by the authors as 'very superficial'; it has no progress measure and no gradual-formation analysis.
Text and molecule data. A general lazy-to-rich switch via initialization scale beyond the MNIST replication and the α-scaling appendix figure.
Not tested. The GPT2-Small and ResNet runs (App. G) report final accuracy and perplexity of the methods, with no delayed-generalization measure.
Not tested: efficient-circuit preference, critical dataset size, and ungrokking.
Floating-point effects outside the softmax cross-entropy sum, and adaptive-optimizer slingshot instabilities (discussed in App. H, not measured).

missing.what: Float32 and float64 test-accuracy curves at the 70% split; needed to complete the dataset-size trend.
Weight-decay sweep: a larger multiplier shortens the delay until wd=8 prevents full generalization; ⊥Grad groks faster than the best weight decay (wd=6).
Logit-scale α: it controls the delay for shallow MSE networks, but for 2-hidden-layer MSE or cross-entropy no α induces grokking.
Logit-norm regularization and a Taylor-approximation softmax each induce grokking without weight decay.
Alternatives to StableMax: softmax temperature scaling (T=1e5) only delays Collapse; label smoothing prevents Collapse but blocks full generalization.
Text only: a too-large Adam ε can stop grokking before Collapse; a custom log_softmax lets learning continue past zero loss.
Gradient absorption errors in the weights grow with vanilla SGD (30% split addition), blocking grokking without learning-rate scheduling.

record.verdict_notes: This study is not one of V7's original sources, but it directly reworks V7. Numerical error is cast as a cause of grokking failing, not of the delay; the delay is placed in loss-driven logit scaling. Fig. 2 rows are figure-only, and states rest on the authors' prose. Rows r4 and r8 (stable-sum fp64) cannot be read and are excluded from verdicts. Row states are given with respect to the delay. For r21 and r22, 'absent' delay means V1 is limited and V7 is supported. The GPT2/ResNet results in App. G report method accuracy only and do not bear on V4.

versions.untested_parts: The study does not establish that the delay grows as the training set shrinks in the usual regularized grokking regime; it measures dataset-size effects on Softmax Collapse without regularization and includes several interventions.
The MNIST experiment tests scaled weights with and without weight decay, not a general lazy-to-rich transition or initialization-scale effects across non-algorithmic settings.
The GPT2-Small experiment reports training/evaluation performance for one epoch, not grokking-like delayed generalization during realistic large-model training.
The study does not test whether an efficient generalizing circuit is favored over memorization, a critical dataset size, or ungrokking below that size.
The study tests Softmax numerical errors and some optimizer settings, but does not comprehensively test adaptive-optimizer instabilities or floating-point limits across implementations.

relation.reason: The study directly measures generalization trajectories under precision, loss, representation and optimizer interventions.

tranche.reason: Controlled interventions distinguish the cause of delayed generalization from numerical failures that prevent it, qualifying existing accounts.

source_check.notes: Appendix G benchmarks GPT2-Small and ResNets but does not establish artifact-controlled realistic-model grokking. The text attributes 100% test accuracy within 400 iterations to Figure 6a, although the panel timescales suggest an inconsistent cross-reference; synthesis-wide counts were not independently checked.

statements.correction: This study: V1 limits_scope for unregularized ordinary-Softmax precision conditions; no grokking at 40%; larger-split generalization can stop at Collapse onset; StableMax restores grokking.
statements.problem: The factual description is supported, but the pooled challenges label overstates this study's condition-dependent result.

statements.correction: MNIST replication: 200 training samples; weights scaled by 100; no decay leads to Collapse and halted generalization; decay mitigates Collapse and permits a delayed improvement; full random-to-near-perfect grokking is not demonstrated.
statements.problem: The MNIST replication tests weight scale 100; it does not establish that unusually large initialization is necessary for cross-entropy MNIST delays.
